title: Amazing Maze
description: A GAME FOR ONE OR TWO, in the disk menu's words. 6 recovered forms; the disk form plays.
versionOrder: Within each capture, save order is retained. Cross-capture ordering is a presentation guess; tape numbers do not establish development dates. Similarity clusters are provisional, and collected saves are not necessarily revisions of one program.

versions.label: AMAZING PROGRAM MAZE
versions.note: validated payload; runtime untested. Ordered lines, consistent pointers, normal end; exact match across original and both-channel variants; runtime untested
versions.unavailableReason: Another recovered save; the site offers one selected player.
versions.startupSource:
5 P$=CHR$(191):D$=CHR$(140):I$=CHR$(191)
10 PRINTTAB(20)"AMAZING PROGRAM"
30 CLS
100 INPUT"WHAT ARE YOUR WIDTH AND LENGTH";H,V
102 IFH<>1ANDV<>1THEN110
104 PRINT"MEANINGLESS DIMENSIONS.  TRY AGAIN.":GOTO100
110 DIM W(H,V),V(H,V)
115 H1=H:V1=V
120 PRINT
130 PRINT
150 PRINT
160 Q=0:Z=0:X=INT(RND(0)*H+1)

versions.label: Amazing Maze (Games Diskette)
versions.note: Complete disk file MAZE.BAS (directory size, ordered records, consistent pointers, end marker). Runs under NEWDOS/80 Disk BASIC from the original disk image; the disk's menu starts it, and it can return there. Runtime limited to the startup check.
